plan.title: Entropy: why hot coffee always cools
plan.description: Entropy measures how spread out energy is in a system. The second law of thermodynamics explains why isolated systems drift toward equilibrium and why some processes never run backwards.

beats.narration: Your coffee never heats itself back up. Why? The answer is a single idea: entropy.
Entropy measures how spread out energy is. Concentrated energy is low entropy. Energy dispersed evenly is high entropy.
The second law says an isolated system's entropy cannot decrease. Heat spreads out, and that makes some processes irreversible.

props.definition: The entropy of an isolated system left to itself cannot decrease with time.

beats.narration: So entropy is why time has a direction: energy spreads, and it never gathers itself back.

props.text: Energy spreads out, and never gathers itself back.
